claims.text: The initial coating is an equiatomic FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloy.
The as-deposited coating has a relatively uniform distribution of its constituent elements without significant surface segregation.
A post-deposition heat treatment can induce Cu diffusion and segregation toward the coating surface.
Heat-treatment-induced Cu segregation promotes formation of a continuous and adherent Cu-oxide tribolayer during high-temperature sliding.
Oxidation kinetics are active during sliding at approximately 600–800°C.
Surface-enriched Cu oxidizes preferentially at high temperature.
Preferential oxidation of surface-enriched Cu produces a stable Cu-oxide layer.
The Cu-oxide layer acts as a thermal barrier.
The Cu-oxide layer reduces direct metal-to-metal contact during sliding.
Reduced direct contact lowers sliding friction.
The Cu-oxide tribolayer suppresses localized plastic deformation, including excessive dislocation activity and grain coarsening.
Dynamic surface passivation by the Cu-oxide tribolayer improves tribological behavior.
Relative to the untreated baseline, the heat-treated coating will have reduced wear-scar depth and volume at 600–800°C.
Relative to the untreated baseline, the heat-treated coating will have lower dislocation density after high-temperature sliding.
Relative to the untreated baseline, the heat-treated coating will exhibit less sliding-induced grain refinement or coarsening.
The untreated coating develops a less pronounced Cu-oxide layer during sliding than the heat-treated coating.
At lower temperatures, limited oxidation may eliminate the proposed wear benefit.
At sufficiently high temperatures, matrix softening may dominate wear and eliminate the proposed benefit.
